_what_this_is: The git pilot policy: five units the estate already meters, from memo 12 and the signed mandate. Document 03 of the insurance-ecosystem pack is the schema; tools/policy.py evaluates this file and nothing else. Numbers are the project lead's placeholders until the ledger re-fits them (GM-D101). Revision 2 adds the levels of enforcement (memo 13) and the files_per_commit unit.

issuer.basis: memo 12, 2 September 2026, and the mandate of 26 August

policyholder.note: the owner of this repository, where the pool lives; every draw names it as acceptor; experience rating lands here

units.meter: git, at pre-commit: the uncompressed size of the blobs the index adds or changes versus HEAD (git diff --cached --raw, then cat-file sizes). A floor, never a bill

exclusion.reason: bytes committed into history are a stock, not a rate: irreversible without rewriting history others hold, and paid by every clone forever. The cap is the vendor's recommended maximum file size, 1 MB (hard limit 100 MB). Not the top of the buffer — the boundary of insurability

units.meter: the ledger: this repository's non-refused commit events today, counted by the evaluator (each commit appends one)
units.note: memo 12 says five to ten a day; ten is taken, and the pool is 2x

units.meter: git, at pre-commit: the number of files the index adds or changes versus HEAD, the ledgers' own files excepted (git diff --cached --name-only)
units.note: memo 13's example ('number of files committed'). Placeholders: a generated site commits many files at once, and the first week of events is what fits them

units.meter: git, at pre-push: the uncompressed size of objects reachable from the pushed sha and not from the remote ref (rev-list --objects, cat-file sizes). The existing push-policy MVP's measurement, unchanged

exclusion.reason: the same stock as bytes_per_commit, at the point where it leaves the machine

units.meter: the ledger: this repository's non-refused push events today, per branch kind
units.pool_scope: per repository, per day, per branch kind
units.note: the push-policy MVP's bands: own 10/20, dev 3/10

units.meter: git, at pre-push: the ref being pushed, against the allow-list of the signed mandate (mandate.py pre-push)

exclusion.reason: a branch is reach, not volume: the mandate governs it and the pool has nothing to say (GM-D87). A push outside the mandate is refused before any byte is counted

reserve.released_by: the issuer, by a decision on a request of kind 'reserve'
reserve.note: the catastrophe layer: no verdict may draw on it; it is subtracted from every pool before the arithmetic

rating.rule: draw frequency is the metric. A pool drawn on most days of the period has the wrong normal band; the response is to raise the band and shrink the pool, never to enlarge the pool

rate_table.note: excluded from the pack; the evaluator never converts between units

does_not_prove: That these numbers fit this repository. They are memo 12's; the push MVP's replay of history says the estate breaches them on every release because the release rewrites every page, and the fix is in the release.
That the hooks are a boundary. They are a setting: the agent can edit them, unset core.hooksPath, or --no-verify. The banner says so.
That bytes measured in the index or before a push are the cost. They are a floor on what is asked.
That one policyholder is a pool. Pooling across policyholders and the correlation card need a second one.
That the levels' consequences are right. Levels 4 and 5 have caught nothing yet; the first catch is what calibrates them.
why: the project lead, 3 Sep 2026, in chat: 'I accept the exhaustion and can you also increase those limits for now, since they are clearly too low for this session (we will review their use and correct values later)' — the first re-fit from the ledger: one day's publication drew the whole pool, a one-line change to a large generator costs the whole file, and a release of this site weighs 250–300 KB. Bands ×4, the exclusion at the vendor's recommended maximum file size, pools ×4, counts ×2. To be reviewed against the ledger

layers._what_this_is: The levels of enforcement (memo 13, doctrine 13). Every event carries the level it was produced at. A catch at a level above the one that should have refused is an INCIDENT, not a volume event: the lower level was bypassed or broken.

1.name: prompt
1.enforced_by: the briefing the session reads at start

2.name: skill / system prompt
2.enforced_by: the push-policy skill and the PreToolUse hook (advisory)
2.consequence: advise, with the same verdict the hook will give

3.name: hook
3.enforced_by: pre-commit, pre-push, the push check — run by git in the agent's own clone
3.consequence: refuse; draws against the pool; a requested draw waits for a decision

4.name: destination
4.enforced_by: a check the agent cannot reach: CI on the pushed ref, a host rule
4.consequence: refuse — and a catch here is an incident: the hook was bypassed or broken. No draw: uninsured by definition; escalate

5.name: post-action, out of band
5.enforced_by: tools/reconcile.py, run by the maintainer or by CI, replaying git against the ledger
5.consequence: a catch is an incident and a candidate for suspension of the licence to operate; the issuer decides
